clue.text: Fantastic old cricketer gets song of praise

parts.note: fantastic in the sense of wonderful or astonishing
W. G. Grace was the famous Victorian England cricketer

explanation.surface: A marvellous veteran cricketer is honoured with a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: W. G. Grace, the bearded Victorian batsman, is the cricketer crosswords reach for when they say 'old cricketer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known hymn by John Newton is a song praising God.

clue.text: After a short time a bee displaced little creatures

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

indicators.note: the letters of 'a bee' are moved out of their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Moments later a bee was knocked off course by tiny creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a short time' reads as one phrase, but its 'a' is a letter of the answer; 'displaced' then gives EBAE from the second 'a' and 'bee'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are single-celled organisms, tiny living things seen under a microscope.

clue.text: Bind? That's what a loud little female, 9, can be!

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
F is the short form of female
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what a noisy small girl could amount to.
explanation.walkthrough: The '9' looks like a reference to the clue at 9 across; it is just the number, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix is to fasten or attach, which is to bind one thing to another.

clue.text: Appeal to umpire — not out!

indicators.note: out here means the letters of 'umpire not' are put out of order

explanation.surface: A fielder pleads with the umpire, who is giving the batsman not out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the cricketing 'not out'; it is the anagram signal for UMPIRE plus NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune someone is to pester or beg them persistently, to appeal to them repeatedly.

clue.text: Article caught in trap is secure

indicators.note: the article is held inside the word for a trap, as if snared

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something caught in a snare is made safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain something is to obtain or win it, to make it yours.

clue.text: I am retained by administrator to supply soldiers

indicators.note: the contraction is held inside the word for an administrator, kept within it

parts.note: a regent administers a kingdom on behalf of a monarch
I'm is the short form of I am

explanation.surface: An official explains that he is kept on to provide troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a military unit made up of many troops.

clue.text: Dance with Georgia after study

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Georgia is placed after the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
GA is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Georgia

explanation.surface: After revising, someone goes dancing with a girl called Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Latin American line dance with people following one another.

clue.text: Old plane fit for flying hanging in part of church

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are suspended inside the church feature

parts.note: a spire is the tapering top of a church tower

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters of 'fit' are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft in good condition for flight is suspended inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit for flying' sounds like airworthiness, but 'flying' shuffles FIT to ITF, and 'hanging in' hangs that inside the church's tower top.
explanation.definitionFit: This British Second World War fighter aircraft is a vintage warplane.

clue.text: Vehicle for insult on cricket field

explanation.surface: A transport used for abuse during a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, sledging is taunting a batsman to break their concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sleigh for snow, and also a cricketer's verbal taunt aimed at an opponent.

clue.text: Bad season for someone's children

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A poor time of year for a person's kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's descendants, their sons and daughters.

clue.text: The French writer's written about mountainous country

indicators.note: about means the French article and the writing tool are read back to front

parts.note: la is French for the, in the feminine
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A French author has written about a Himalayan land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the French article and the pen together; the feminine 'la' is needed here, not 'le'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan kingdom contains Everest and many of the world's highest peaks.

clue.text: Old enemies of Britain — about ten fighters

indicators.note: about here means the old enemies go around the ten

parts.note: the Boers fought Britain in the South African wars
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A historical note about some of Britain's former foes numbering ten.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Boxer rebellion, but the old enemies are the BOERS, wrapped around X.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are pugilists, people who fight in the ring.

clue.text: Firmly pressed, one politician did something

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
to act is to do something, take action

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a single MP finally took action.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impacted is packed in tightly, wedged hard together.

clue.text: Afraid when fellow's discharged lengthy rebuke

indicators.note: discharged means the abbreviation for fellow is sent away from the word

parts.note: fearful means afraid

explanation.surface: Someone frightened when a man is released gets a long telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is a long scolding or tirade that someone has to listen to.

clue.text: Vehicle running into animal completely somersaulted, went back over

indicators.note: the whole combination turns head over heels, so it is read backwards
the vehicle goes inside the animal, as if crashing into it

parts.note: a deer is an animal
a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A cart crashes into a deer and flips over, then retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running into' gives DECARTER (the cart inside the animal), and 'completely somersaulted' flips that whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace one's steps is to go back over the same route again.

clue.text: Being idle ain't vice surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of 'ain't vice' come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Laziness, the speaker claims unexpectedly, is not a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idle means not doing anything, lacking activity.

clue.text: Carriage getting about with gusto before meeting obstruction

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
brio is vigour or gusto
a let is an obstruction or hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A coach travelling enthusiastically runs into a roadblock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood.

clue.text: Country friend entertaining former occupant of cliveden?

indicators.note: entertaining means the friend holds the former occupant inside, as a host does

parts.note: a pal is a friend
the Astor family, notably Nancy Astor, lived at Cliveden House

explanation.surface: A friend hosts an aristocrat who once lived at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliveden is a stately home in Buckinghamshire once owned by the Astor family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life, the countryside and its shepherds.

clue.text: As good as secured where the shopping is?

explanation.surface: Shopping is safely bagged up and the deal is done.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means certain to be won, and literally names the sack holding purchases.

clue.text: Prevail on popular Italian dictator

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini

explanation.surface: A fashionable Italian dictator wins someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade them, to prevail upon them to act.

clue.text: Superior woman who must deal with the others in order

definitions.text: Superior woman who must deal with the others in order

parts.words: Superior woman who must deal with the others in order
parts.note: a Mother Superior runs the other nuns of a religious order, though the surface suggests a bossy woman tidying up

explanation.surface: A haughty woman has to sort everyone else out neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the head of a convent, the senior nun overseeing the community.

clue.text: Overdose could make fustier

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of 'fustier' can be reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Too much of something might leave things more musty.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, too much of something.

clue.text: These pose problem in old house — it can be a game!

definitions.text: These pose problem in old house

explanation.surface: Cold air in an old house, and a board game to pass the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts are cold currents of air in a building and also a board game known in the US as checkers.

clue.text: Character from Athens setting up a male periodical

indicators.note: in a down clue setting up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: Someone from Athens launches a men's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the third letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Food for breakfast? This person's still asleep!

explanation.surface: A smoked fish breakfast while someone is still dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a smoked herring, and also one who kips, a sleeper.

clue.text: Spot shoestring under piano

indicators.note: in a down clue the lace sits below the piano abbreviation

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
a shoestring is a lace

explanation.surface: A tiny spot found beneath a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A place is a location or spot.

clue.text: Guy possibly spending Sunday on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue the Sunday abbreviation sits on top of the river

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A man perhaps spends his Sunday on a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope that steadies a tent or mast, and a stay is the same kind of supporting rope.

clue.text: Cold sheets may be best

parts.note: C is short for cold, as on taps
a ream is a quantity of sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Chilly bedding might be the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream is the elite, the finest part of anything.

clue.text: I subsequently returned, had a meal, and hit back

indicators.note: returned means 'I later' comes back in reverse order

parts.note: later means subsequently
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Someone comes home afterwards, eats, and then strikes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to take revenge, to strike back at an attacker.

clue.text: A way to offer private medical treatment

definitions.text: A way to offer private medical treatment

parts.words: A way to offer private medical treatment
parts.note: the way is literally a road, the London one famous for private doctors' consulting rooms

explanation.surface: A method for providing private healthcare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' reads as a method, but it is a street; London's Harley Street is lined with private doctors' practices.
explanation.definitionFit: This London thoroughfare is famous for private specialist clinics.
